entities.summary: Michelangelo Cerquozzi, known as Michelangelo delle Battaglie was an Italian Baroque painter known for his genre scenes, battle pictures, small religious and mythological works and still lifes. His genre scenes were influenced by the work of the Flemish and Dutch genre artists referred to as the Bamboccianti active in Rome who created small cabinet paintings and prints of the everyday life of the lower classes in Rome and its countryside. One of the leading battle painters active in Italy in the first half of the 17th century, Michelangelo Cerquozzi earned the nickname 'Michelangelo delle Battaglie'.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Michelangelo Cerquozzi's battle paintings had a significant regional impact in Italy during the first half of the 17th century, influencing the development of Italian art and contributing to the country's artistic heritage. His work also reflects the cultural and social changes brought about by the Baroque period.
